Chapter Eight: Sustaining Prayer in Seasons of Dryness and Doubt
Let’s be honest—no matter how devoted we are, there are times when prayer just... feels hard. Maybe it seems empty, or you wonder if anyone’s listening. If you’ve ever been there, you’re definitely not alone.
Ancient Christian wisdom doesn’t hide from this reality. In fact, it offers gentle guidance for navigating those moments when your spiritual life feels dry or uncertain.
Here’s something to really pay attention to: these tough seasons are completely normal. Just like in any relationship, there are times of distance or silence. The important thing isn’t to give up—it’s to keep showing up, even when it feels like nothing’s happening. Trust that God is still present, even if you don’t feel it right now.
So, what can you do when prayer feels impossible? Here are a few gentle strategies:
First, you can lean on structured prayers, or turn to the psalms, especially when your own words just won’t come. Sometimes, letting ancient words carry you makes all the difference.
Or, you might want to shorten your practice. Focus on a single phrase, or even a simple breath prayer—something small and manageable.
And don’t forget, you can invite others to pray for you. Sharing your struggles honestly can be a huge relief, and sometimes, letting someone else carry your prayers is exactly what you need.
Think of it like a tree in winter. The branches might look bare and lifeless, but the roots are still reaching deep, drawing nourishment. In the same way, sticking with prayer during dry seasons actually strengthens your roots—your trust, your perseverance.
It’s also helpful to remember: prayer isn’t measured by emotional highs or visible results. Just turning toward God, even in a faltering way, is an act of faith. Over time, these small, steady acts can create space for new growth and renewal.
Now, what about doubt? You might be surprised—doubt isn’t the enemy of prayer. In fact, it’s often a companion on the journey. The psalms are full of questions, complaints, even cries for help. Bringing your doubts into prayer, instead of hiding them, opens the door to deeper honesty and, eventually, transformation.
So, here’s the key takeaway: sustaining prayer in hard times is really about embracing grace. You don’t have to pretend, or put on a show. The invitation is to come exactly as you are, trusting that God meets you in weakness just as much as in strength.
